wy_wolfs_head.blurb: Wolfs Head is a granite peak on the northwest side of the Cirque of the Towers in the Wind River Range, close to Pingora. The dozen listed routes are almost all long alpine-style trad lines, from a moderate 5.6 ridge up through the 5.9 to 5.12 range, with a single 5.13 at the top end. The south face is steep and crack-focused, with slabs, roofs and finger to fist cracks, while the ridge is a mellower scramble-and-rope day. Expect a very long walk in, a full rack, and afternoon thunderstorms in summer, so start early.

wy_snag_wall.blurb: Snag Wall is a small dolomite wall in Tongue River Canyon in the Eastern Bighorns, west of Sheridan. Its eleven routes split about evenly between bolted sport lines and trad cracks, running from easy 5.7s through the 5.9 and 5.10 range up to a couple of 5.11s. The wall sits a very short walk off the canyon trail and is tucked out of sight from it, which makes it a handy spot for a quick session. The canyon's south-facing walls run hot in summer and can be pleasantly warm in late winter and early spring, and crowds stay light.

wy_gorilla_rock.blurb: Gorilla Rock is a compact crag in Vedauwoo, near Laramie, packed with cracks. Many are wide, but a couple are thin, and nearly all of the eleven climbs are trad, mostly between 5.9 and 5.11, with a few boulder problems as well. The routes sit in two side-by-side alcoves behind big boulders. The walk in is long, vague and pathless through forest, so few climbers make the effort and it feels like a locals' spot. Bring a trad rack and be ready to navigate by eye.

wy_citadel_crag.blurb: Citadel Crag is a quiet single-pitch crag in the Vedauwoo area of Medicine Bow National Forest, near Laramie, set apart from the busier crack corridors. It holds eleven climbs, mostly trad with a couple of bolted lines and one boulder problem. Grades run from approachable 5.8 up to harder 5.10 and 5.11 climbs, so it suits climbers comfortable leading cracks. The face takes the sun, making mornings cool and afternoons warm, and summer thunderstorms are worth planning around. Bring a standard trad rack and quickdraws.

wy_mouth_the.blurb: The Mouth is where Clark's Fork Canyon opens out, about 25 miles north of Cody, with limestone slabs that rise thousands of feet. It is a place for long, committing days: mostly trad and alpine multi-pitch lines with some bolted sport climbing and a pair of aid routes. Grades span easy fifth class through the 5.10s to a few 5.11 and 5.12 pitches. Most routes face east, so the walls get morning sun and fall into shade by early afternoon. It is very windy, and storms arrive from the west and are hard to spot.

wy_disappointment_peak.blurb: Disappointment Peak is an 11,600-foot summit in the Cathedral Group of Grand Teton National Park, rising north of Garnet Canyon. Most of the climbing is alpine-style trad on the flanks, from a moderate fifth-class ridge to several multi-pitch lines in the 5.8 to 5.10 range and a few much harder test pieces up to 5.12. There is also one steep ice route and a class 4 option. Expect long mountain days with a hike in, a full rack, and a summer season.

wy_home_on_the_range_rock_temporary_name.blurb: This is the main cliff in the Coyote Rocks group at Vedauwoo, near Laramie, spotted from the road by an arching crack on its left side. Most of the eleven climbs are trad, with a few bolted lines and a hard top-rope boulder problem. The spread is wide: easy 5.5 and 5.6 climbs, a middle band in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, and a very hard 5.13 crack at the top. The surrounding Coyote Rocks area is better known for bouldering.
